source.title: Differentially Private Sharpness-Aware Training
source.authors: Jinseong Park; Hoki Kim; Yu-Jin Choi; Jaewoo Lee

record.tranche_reason: Tests sharpness-aware training and generalization-related measurements in differentially private learning, an extension beyond the claim versions’ stated standard-training settings.
record.gate_note: The paper measures conventional Hessian sharpness, gradient effects of clipping and noise, and train/test loss behavior under DP training. It does not test the claim versions’ specified settings. Cited findings from prior work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: Appendix G.3, Table 11 directly compares held-out accuracy of DP-Adam and DP-SGD with and without momentum, testing V4 in a differentially private setting. The sharpness results do not test V7's magnitude-aware measure or its ranking of generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the conclusion: seeking flat minima can mitigate clipping and noise effects, and DP-SAT improves private training performance with the same privacy guarantee and approximately the same computational cost as DP-SGD. Fine-tuning improvements are generally marginal and are not universal.
record.recipe_differences: Studies differentially private training rather than the claim versions’ standard training settings; compares DP-SGD, DP-SAM and DP-SAT and measures conventional Hessian sharpness and train/test loss behavior.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that the DP-SAT benefit depends on selecting an appropriate radius ρ; too small or too large a radius may fail to improve performance, and accuracy has high variance and fluctuating trends. They also report gradient-direction similarities vary with clipping value and batch size.

fits_no_version.finding: The clipped fraction on MNIST decreases from 0.86 at epoch 1 to 0.22 at epoch 10 and 0.14 at epoch 40.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Individual-gradient clipping becomes less frequent over the studied DP-SGD training run while remaining nonzero.

fits_no_version.finding: On the constructed loss surface, lower Hessian sharpness accompanies smaller noise-induced gradient differences.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Flatter regions can reduce the effect of update noise in the studied toy optimization problem.

fits_no_version.finding: DP-SAT has lower Hessian maximum eigenvalue and eigenvalue ratio than DP-SGD, and the interpolation analysis reports lower training and test errors at its endpoint.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed private training method combines lower conventional Hessian sharpness with improved predictive performance in the studied comparison.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 202, 2023
record.problems: Evidence concerns differentially private learning, not the claim versions’ standard-training settings. The toy comparison is illustrative; Hessian eigenspectrum results are presented in figures without uncertainty estimates in the supplied text; the train/test loss relationship is qualitative.
record.rows_left_out: No additional direct measurements bearing on the claim versions were identified. Accuracy tables compare private training methods but do not measure the specified generalization gaps or interventions in V1–V8.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the corresponding natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.

Systematic tuning-budget comparisons, broader tuning, learning-rate decay schedules, equal-training-performance comparisons, decoupled weight decay, optimizer switching, and language benchmarks. Table 11 reports selected learning rates without documenting a matched optimizer search.
Held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes. Appendix F measures gradient similarity, not held-out performance.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, generalization-gap rankings at similarly low training loss, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing examples selected by label memorization and comparing retraining accuracy with random removal.

missing.what: Add subject-by-dataset-by-privacy-budget rows comparing DP-Adam with DP-SGD at momentum 0 and 0.9. Adam accuracies for ε = 1, 2, 3 are MNIST 97.96, 98.54, 98.68%; FashionMNIST 84.85, 87.17, 87.84%; CIFAR-10 61.75, 66.68, 68.86%. Corresponding momentum-SGD values are 97.77, 98.60, 98.70%; 84.62, 86.99, 87.97%; 59.42, 66.30, 68.43%. Without momentum they are 97.62, 97.65, 97.70%; 80.80, 81.55, 82.03%; 56.15, 56.59, 56.87%. Preserve the table's uncertainties and record Adam's learning rate of 0.0002 and SGD's 2.0.
missing.locator: Appendix G.3, Table 11; Appendix C.1 and Table 5

record.verdict_notes: The decisive omission is Table 11, not the change from standard to private training itself. Differential privacy supplies a new test setting for V4; conventional Hessian sharpness remains a different measure from V7. Verdicts use the supplied text because the relevant optimizer-comparison rows are missing. This study is not an original source for V4.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under standard training.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation under standard training.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers under standard training.
Adaptive optimizer comparisons and tuning under standard training.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout and weight-decay comparisons in the stated regimes.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness comparisons among networks at similarly low training loss, and comparisons to norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: DP-SGD on MNIST
rows.operation_detail: Measured the proportion of individual gradients with norm above clipping threshold over training.
rows.note: The paper says the proportion is high early in training.
rows.check: The clipping proportion is correctly reported, but it measures no claim version; observed is not a claim-relative state.

rows.subject: DP-SGD on MNIST
rows.operation_detail: Measured the proportion of individual gradients with norm above clipping threshold over training.
rows.note: The paper says the proportion diminishes as training proceeds.
rows.check: The clipping proportion is correctly reported, but it measures no claim version.

rows.subject: DP-SGD on MNIST
rows.operation_detail: Measured the proportion of individual gradients with norm above clipping threshold over training.
rows.note: The paper says some individual gradients are still clipped at the end.
rows.check: The clipping proportion is correctly reported, but it measures no claim version.

rows.subject: Toy example with flat and sharp minima
rows.operation_detail: Measured Hessian sharpness and gradient difference between updates with and without noise during gradient descent.

conditions.value: same level added at each step

rows.value: The paper reports a positive correlation during training; the flat minimum has lower sharpness and lower gradient difference than the sharp minimum.
rows.note: Toy setting; this does not test the claim versions’ natural-label standard-training regimes.
rows.check: This is a constructed loss surface, not a toy network measuring generalization. Noise-induced gradient differences cannot establish V7.

rows.subject: DP-SGD and DP-SAT trained models on CIFAR-10
rows.operation_detail: Compared Hessian eigenspectrum sharpness measures of trained models.
rows.measure: Hessian maximum eigenvalue λmax and ratio λmax/λ5
rows.note: The text states that both measures are smaller for DP-SAT.
rows.check: The numbers are correct, but this comparison of the proposed method with DP-SGD uses unscaled Hessian measures, not V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure. Exclude from claim-evidence rows.

rows.subject: DP-SGD and DP-SAT trained models
rows.operation_detail: Compared training and test loss surfaces using linear interpolation between models.
rows.measure: Similarity of training and test losses; training and test errors
rows.value: The paper reports higher similarity between training and test losses under DP training and lower training and test errors for DP-SAT; function shape is described as strongly correlated with generalization performance.
rows.note: Qualitative result; the supplied text gives no exact loss-gap values.
rows.check: Figure 9 interpolates between one DP-SGD endpoint and one DP-SAT endpoint, rather than comparing separate interpolation experiments. Its qualitative loss and accuracy curves do not establish magnitude-aware sharpness rankings among similarly fitted networks. Exclude from claim-evidence rows.

relationships.condition: Private DPNAS image classifiers; Adam versus SGD without momentum; MNIST, FashionMNIST, and CIFAR-10 at ε = 1, 2, 3.
relationships.reason: Missing Table 11 rows: DP-Adam has higher mean test accuracy in all nine comparisons, by 0.34–0.98, 4.05–5.81, and 5.60–11.99 percentage points respectively; this challenges an adaptive-optimizer disadvantage in these settings.
relationships.display_finding: Differentially private Adam (DP-Adam) reportedly achieved higher mean test accuracy than differentially private stochastic gradient descent (DP-SGD) without momentum in all nine comparisons. These comparisons remain unverified.
